Subject: Follow-up: GigaCare PII handling for chat prompts — confirmation & rollout gates

Hi Sara / Tom — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete asks so we stay aligned.

What we covered (short):
- Use case: agent/chat workflows that may include PHI/PII in user messages and model outputs.
- Primary constraint: data residency in US (preferred us-east), strong auditability, and optional customer-managed keys for encryption.

Open asks from GigaCare for us to confirm:
1) Exactly what gets persisted by default (prompt inputs, model outputs, telemetry/trace).
2) Retention windows available and per-environment/route overrides (can you set TTL=0 / session-only?).
3) Audit/logging controls available (token-level logs vs aggregated telemetry, masking options).
4) KMS/HSM options and whether a CMK in the customer's AWS account is supported for hosted/dedicated/private.
5) Any SOC2 / pen-test artifacts we can share ahead of security review.

Attached: redwood_data_handling_summary.pdf (summary of options) and a link to our runbook for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Proposed next steps:
- Ben and I will run a short “configuration matrix” doc that maps your requirements to Hosted / Dedicated / Private options by EOD Wed.
- Security team: can we schedule a 30–45 min technical call this week to walk through SOC2 evidence and KMS integration?
- If agreed, propose a 2-week canary in us-east with the prompt TTL set to 0 for the first 48 hours, then move to 30-day outputs for analytics.

Thanks — Marcus
Marcus Lin

Subject: Re: Follow-up: GigaCare PII handling for chat prompts — confirmation & rollout gates

Thanks Marcus — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side after talking with security: 
- Residency: must be in the US (us-east preferred).
- Retention: we prefer prompt inputs not be stored by default — TTL=0/session-only for PII-containing prompts is ideal. If storage is required for troubleshooting, it must be opt-in and limited to 30 days.
- Outputs: model responses that include PHI/PII should be configurable; default for our prod workloads should be 30 days if persisted.
- Audit logs: we require request/response-level audit logs (redacted for tokens) for at least 90 days; access must be auditable.
- Encryption: we require support for customer-managed CMK in our AWS account for any persisted data.

Attaching our security questionnaire (GigaCare_Security_Questionnaire.pdf). We'll expect a short written mapping to your features and where they apply (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Also please confirm whether the hosted API supports immediate "no-persist" flag or if that requires Dedicated/Private.

Tom Lowe
Product Security Lead, GigaCare
Tom.Lowe@gigacare.com

Subject: Re: Follow-up: GigaCare PII handling for chat prompts — confirmation & rollout gates

Sara / Tom — thanks for the clear asks. I wanted to put concrete, actionable answers on the table so your security and procurement teams have something to review. High level (defaults vs options):

Hosted API (standard):
- Persistence: by default Redwood stores request/response pairs for 30 days for debugging/quality; for enterprise customers we can enable a "no-persist" mode at the route level that prevents storing prompt content (session-only). This is available today via a per-API-credential flag.
- TTL: configurable per-route from 0 (session-only) up to 90 days.
- Audit logs: aggregated telemetry retained 365 days; request/response audit logs available as an add-on for 90 days with masking (tokens hashed, PII redaction rules applied).
- KMS: Hosted supports envelope encryption; customer CMKs are supported in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, we offer KMIP/KMS integrations in our enterprise plan (we will map requirements in the doc).

Dedicated / Private (recommended for strict controls):
- Persistence: full control — can set TTL=0, store only aggregated metrics, or persist outputs in your VPC storage.
- KMS: supports customer-managed CMK (in your AWS account) and HSM for on-prem installs.
- Audit logs: more granular logs (token-level events) can be exported to your SIEM; retention and access controls are configurable.

Attachments: redwood_data_handling_summary.pdf (short matrix) — covers above and callouts for gating a canary.

Suggested next steps (short):
1) Security call: schedule 45 min with your security team and our infra engineers (I propose Thu 3/14 10:00–10:45 PT).
2) Provide SOC2 Type II and pen-test redacted artifacts — I can share a secure Drive link once we have an NDA in place.
3) Canary plan: deploy a 2-week canary in us-east; initial config: prompt TTL=0 for first 48 hours, outputs disabled for analytics for first 24 hours, then outputs=30 days if no issues.

If that aligns, I’ll circulate a short MOP (method of procedure) and timeline.

—Ben
